answer: Tie each agent to one council allotment plot. The council leases a numbered plot to one person for 50 pounds a year and binds the plot to the agent key. Monthly the agent posts a dated photo of its plot with copper tags in frame, and an officer spot-checks one plot in ten. A terrace of plots on one hillside exposes clones: identical photos from one hand fail the check. Forging 1,000 identities means 1,000 plots at 50,000 pounds a year plus 12,000 hours of tending, so the farm costs more than it earns. Like a forge that tempers one blade at a time, each plot proves one real gardener.
